package_info.why_malicious: A malicious version of the 'conventional-changelog' npm package was uploaded after the maintainer's credentials were compromised. This version included code that, when installed or executed, downloaded and ran a Monero cryptocurrency miner without user consent. This resulted in unauthorized use of system resources for mining, potential exfiltration of further data, and risk of downstream supply chain compromise.

execution_context.trigger: runtime (when the package entry point is executed, e.g., during build or CLI usage)
execution_context.file_location: main package entry point (e.g., index.js or similar, as modified in the malicious version)
required_permissions: filesystem (to write miner files and logs)
process (to spawn shell and miner processes)
network (to download miner script and connect to mining pool)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code spawns a shell process that downloads a remote shell script from a hardcoded URL using curl, pipes it to sh for execution, resulting in the installation and execution of a Monero cryptocurrency miner, which hijacks system resources for unauthorized mining.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The code initiates a remote script download and executes it without user knowledge or consent, a hallmark of malware delivery. The use of 'curl' piped to 'sh' is a common technique for fetching and running malicious payloads, in this case a cryptocurrency miner.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate npm packages should never download and execute remote code at runtime, especially not to install or run cryptocurrency mining software. Such behavior is outside the scope of any expected package functionality.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Some legitimate packages may fetch dependencies or perform updates during installation, but they do not execute arbitrary remote scripts or install unrelated binaries such as miners. Automated update scripts are typically signed, versioned, and do not run hidden processes.
key_indicators: Remote script download and execution via shell (e.g., 'curl ... | sh')
Hardcoded external URL for script delivery
Creation or execution of miner binaries (e.g., xmrig, miner.sh)
No user notification or opt-in for code execution
Spawning of long-running, high-CPU processes after package use

attack_chain.action: Attacker compromises maintainer credentials and uploads a malicious version of the 'conventional-changelog' package to npm.
attack_chain.leads_to: Malicious code is distributed to users via npm install.

attack_chain.action: User installs or builds a project that depends on the malicious package, causing the package entry point to execute.
attack_chain.leads_to: Malicious code is executed on the user's system.

attack_chain.action: Malicious code downloads and executes a Monero miner by fetching and running a remote shell script.
attack_chain.leads_to: System resources are hijacked for unauthorized cryptocurrency mining.

attack_chain.action: Potential further distribution occurs if downstream users or customers install the compromised package as a dependency.
attack_chain.leads_to: Wider spread of the malicious miner across the supply chain.

behavioral_signatures: Unexpected remote script execution (e.g., 'curl ... | sh') during package runtime or build
Installation or execution of cryptocurrency mining software (e.g., xmrig, miner.sh) initiated by node or shell processes
Sustained high CPU usage by node, shell, or miner processes after package install or use
file_indicators: Presence of miner binaries (e.g., xmrig, miner.sh) in node_modules, project directories, or system temp folders
Unexpected modifications or additions to package entry points (e.g., index.js) that include remote script execution code
network_indicators: Outbound HTTP/HTTPS connections to hardcoded or suspicious domains (e.g., malicious-domain.com) for script download
Network traffic to known Monero mining pool endpoints following package execution
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor npm packages for code that downloads and executes remote scripts, especially via shell commands like 'curl ... | sh'. Flag any package that installs or runs binaries unrelated to its documented functionality, particularly known miner binaries. Watch for unexplained spikes in CPU usage after installing or running new packages, and scan for outbound connections to mining pool domains or suspicious script hosts. Automated static analysis should alert on hardcoded URLs and shell execution patterns in package entry points.
